results.proposal_summary: The ADF Climate Action Window is an initiative of the African Development Fund (concessional arm of the African Development Bank Group) established under its 16th replenishment cycle to help fill the climate finance gap for low-income African countries. Resources are allocated across three sub-windows: 75% for adaptation, 15% for mitigation, and 10% for technical assistance, covering six thematic sectors including agriculture and food security, water security, climate information, green transport, green energy, and green finance. The programme targets ADF-eligible sub-Saharan and North African countries, offering a large grant component to minimise debt distress. This landing page does not present a currently open call with a defined deadline; eligible applicant types and specific grant amounts are not specified on this page.

results.proposal_summary: The UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) has launched a call for expressions of interest for the Sudan Stability Programme (SSP), a £39 million, 5-year programme (2026–2031) aimed at ending hostilities in Sudan. This call relates to delivery of outcomes 2 and 3 (civilian dialogue, local governance, and conflict management), with an indicative value of up to £25 million. Eligible lead applicants include international and non-governmental organisations, Sudanese civil society organisations, United Nations agencies, not-for-profit organisations, and academic institutions; for-profit organisations may only participate as downstream partners. Applicants need not be based in the UK or Sudan but must demonstrate the ability to manage risk and deliver in the Sudanese context. The expression of interest (maximum 3,000 words plus budget) must be submitted to FCDO by 11:59pm Eastern Africa Time on 16 October 2026. No co-financing requirement is stated.
results.ilo_match_evidence: The programme addresses civilian protection, social cohesion, local governance, and inclusion of women and girls in conflict settings in Sudan, which aligns with ILO's decent work in crisis and post-crisis situations mandate, though it is primarily a peace and stability programme rather than a core labour/employment intervention.

results.proposal_summary: Expertise France (under the NUMÜ/WATANI programme) invites Tunisian organizations to apply for grants of €50,000–€200,000 to provide business acceleration, coaching, training, market access, and innovation support services to startups, SMEs, and other enterprises with at least 1 year of existence in Tunisia. The call is open on a rolling basis from 14 April 2026 until 30 September 2028 or until funds are exhausted. Applications are submitted via the POPS online platform.
results.ilo_match_evidence: While the call mentions employment creation indicators (jobs created in supported enterprises), its primary focus is private-sector SME acceleration and enterprise support services in Tunisia, which falls outside core ILO mandate areas of labour standards, social protection, social dialogue, and decent work policy.
